newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF mission to arrive Moscow on Wednesday - Yasin.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to arrive Moscow on Wednesday - Yasin.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission will arrive in Moscow on Wednesday to finalise talks on Russia's 1997 economic programme, former Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Monday.

"The most difficult problems concern the budget, its expenses and taxes," Yasin, who said First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais had authorised him to continue talks with the IMF, told a news conference.
"These problems will be discussed on Wednesday when the (IMF) mission arrives in Moscow."
Yasin was not on the government list after a recent reshuffle but is expected by some to be a minister without portfolio in the new government.
The 1997 economic plan will outline plans for structural reforms.

Russian officials say the IMF is particularly insistent on reforming Russian natural monopolies such as national power utility Unified Energy System (UES), the Railway Ministry and Gazprom natural gas producer monopoly.
New First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has critisised monopolies for high prices, which he said hinder economic growth.
